AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry.summary: The libraries supply only generic infrastructure that these stages would consume: Mathlib's Proj of a graded ring with affine charts and properness over Spec A₀, the Grassmannian as a functor of points (not yet shown representable), a numerical Hilbert polynomial, Zariski-local representability, relatively representable morphisms with a diagonal criterion, fibered categories and pseudofunctor stacks with descent data, fpqc/étale topologies with descent of morphism properties, faithfully flat descent of modules over affine bases, relative normalization, scheme-theoretic images and the Rees algebra; Tau Ceti adds absolute cohomology and invertible sheaves on a scheme, fppf quotients of affine groups, and the separable and purely inseparable cases of finite normalization. Genuinely missing: projective bundles over a general base with O(1), ampleness and projective morphisms, representable Grassmannian and flag schemes, Hilbert, Quot, Hom and Isom schemes, Chow's lemma, algebraic spaces and Weil restriction, effective descent of quasi-coherent sheaves and affine objects, stacks fibred in groupoids with stackification, atlases and algebraicity, coarse spaces and rigidification, deformation theory with Artin representability and algebraization, relative coherent cohomology with base change (which the document assumes is already supplied), the relative Picard functor, excellent rings, and all of characteristic-zero resolution and SNC compactification (R09.7–R09.7d).

targets.target: Proper-flat coherent cohomology and cohomology-and-base-change beyond curves (finite presentation, Tor-amplitude, flatness hypotheses)
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines only absolute cohomology H^i(X, M) of an O_X-module (Ext from the constant sheaf, with long exact and Mayer-Vietoris sequences) and Mathlib has pushforward/pullback of O_X-modules. There are no higher direct images, finiteness for proper morphisms, base-change maps, semicontinuity, Tor-amplitude or perfect complexes, although the README assumes relative coherent cohomology is supplied by the existing portfolio.

targets.target: Relative degree-zero Picard functor and its representability criteria (algebraic space, effectivity)
targets.note: Only the Picard group of a commutative ring (Mathlib) and invertible sheaves with their isomorphism-class group on a single scheme (Tau Ceti) exist. There is no relative Picard functor, no sheafification of it, no Pic^0 and no representability statement.

targets.target: Artin's representability criterion itself (statement and proof)
targets.note: No Artin representability theorem exists, and there are no algebraic spaces or algebraic stacks to state it for.

targets.target: Artin input: limit preservation
targets.note: Mathlib proves that Hom_S(-, X) sends cofiltered limits of qcqs S-schemes with affine transition maps to colimits when X is locally of finite presentation (Stacks 01ZC), and gives Noetherian models of smooth algebras (Algebra.Smooth.exists_finiteType, not in declarations.tsv: public modifier). Limit preservation for moduli functors or stacks (e.g. the Picard functor) is neither formulated nor proved.

targets.target: Artin input: representable diagonal
targets.note: Mathlib defines relatively representable morphisms and proves the diagonal of an object is relatively representable iff every map from a representable is (for a full functor preserving binary products and pullbacks), which covers set-valued functors. Missing: the stack version via Isom sheaves and its verification for the Picard functor or PEL moduli.

targets.target: Artin input: deformation and obstruction functors/theories
targets.note: Only the dual-number/derivation dictionary for lifts of algebra maps (Tau Ceti) and formal smoothness (Mathlib) exist; there are no deformation categories, tangent-obstruction theories or obstruction spaces.

targets.target: Artin input: openness of versality
targets.note: No notion of versal object or versality locus exists in either library.

targets.target: Artin input: algebraization/effectivity of formal objects
targets.note: Only adic completions of rings and modules are available; there are no formal schemes, no Grothendieck existence theorem and no effectivity statements.

targets.target: Verification of the Artin inputs in every PEL application
targets.note: Application-level obligation; nothing exists because neither the PEL moduli functors nor the criterion are formalized.

targets.target: Analytification of étale presentations and descent of local-isomorphism comparisons
targets.note: Neither library has complex-analytic spaces or an analytification functor for schemes; Tau Ceti's analytic geometry is non-archimedean (adic spaces).

targets.target: Finite normalization under excellence
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the relative normalization of a qcqs morphism and proves finiteness of the integral closure of an integrally closed Noetherian domain in a finite separable extension; Tau Ceti adds the purely inseparable case over a polynomial ring over a field and Krull-Akizuki (Noetherian, not finite). Missing: excellent/Nagata (Japanese) rings and the theorem that the normalization of a reduced excellent scheme is finite.

duplicates.note: Also plans proper-flat finitely presented pushforward, flat base change, cohomology and base change and semicontinuity, the base-change package this layer extends beyond curves.
Also plans coherent pushforward under proper morphisms over locally Noetherian bases with the full cohomology-and-base-change theorem, Grauert's theorem and semicontinuity.
Also plans the fppf relative Picard functor, its rigidification, Pic^0 and representability (for curves), overlapping the relative Picard representability criteria.
States the construction of the relative degree-zero Picard functor as an algebraic space, the same object whose representability this layer is to construct.
Restates 'extend analytification to the étale presentations' and the descent of local-isomorphism comparisons for its generic-fibre moduli space.
Also lists normalization under the applicable excellence hypotheses as an internal proof task.

targets.target: Projective bundles P(E) with invertible-quotient universal property
targets.note: Mathlib builds Proj of an N-graded ring as a scheme over Spec A_0 with basic-open affine charts, functoriality (Proj.map), separatedness and (unnamed instance) properness when A is of finite type over A_0, plus maps X -> Proj A from ring maps into global sections whose irrelevant ideal generates; Tau Ceti grades Sym(M). Missing: relative Proj / P(E) over a non-affine base, the universal property via invertible quotients of E, and a named P^n_S.

targets.target: Grassmannians with universal quotient, representability and base-change laws
targets.note: Mathlib defines G(k, M; R) as submodules with finite projective quotient of constant rank k, and the functor A -> G(k, A ⊗ M; A) on R-algebras with base-change maps. Missing (listed as TODO in the file): affine charts, representability by a scheme, the universal quotient sheaf, and Grassmannians of quasi-coherent sheaves over a general base.

targets.target: Flag schemes with universal filtrations
targets.note: No flag functor or flag scheme exists; Mathlib's Flag and Module.Basis.flag are order-theoretic chains of submodules, not parameter spaces.

targets.target: Universal sheaves (O(1), universal quotients/subbundles) and base-change laws
targets.note: There are no Serre twisting sheaves O(n) on Proj, no universal quotient on a Grassmannian and no base-change isomorphism for Proj; only pointwise base-change maps of the Grassmannian functor exist.

targets.target: Relative ampleness and very ampleness
targets.note: Neither library defines ample or very ample invertible sheaves, or projective/quasi-projective morphisms; Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves and their class group only.

targets.target: Hilbert polynomials
targets.note: Mathlib's hilbertPoly p d is the polynomial eventually computing the coefficients of p/(1-X)^d over a characteristic-zero field, and Tau Ceti has a truncated Euler characteristic of cohomology over a field. Missing: Hilbert-Serre for finitely generated graded modules (a Mathlib TODO) and the Hilbert polynomial n -> chi(F(n)) of a coherent sheaf on a projective scheme.

targets.target: Boundedness statements in the Noetherian setting
targets.note: No Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, Serre vanishing, global generation or boundedness-of-families results exist.

targets.target: Closedness of the equations defining invariant subbundles and Frobenius-stable lattices
targets.note: Only isocrystals over the fraction field of Witt vectors exist; there are no closed-subscheme statements for invariant subbundles or Frobenius-stable lattices.

targets.target: Required checks: projective space as line quotients; a rank-one Grassmannian
targets.note: Module.Grassmannian with k = 1 is the functor of rank-one locally free quotients, but its identification with Proj of a polynomial ring (projective space) is not proved.

duplicates.note: Constructs the relative Grassmannian scheme of locally free rank-N quotients with affine charts, gluing and universal property.
Also plans relative ampleness, projective morphisms and relative Proj of a finitely generated graded quasi-coherent algebra.
Also plans relative Proj, the construction underlying projective bundles.

targets.target: Hilbert functor and Hilbert scheme with fixed Hilbert polynomial (representability)
targets.note: There is no Hilbert functor of flat closed subschemes and no Hilbert scheme; only the Zariski-local representability criterion (Stacks 01JJ) and the numerical Hilbert polynomial are available.

targets.target: Quot functor and Quot scheme (representability)
targets.note: No Quot functor exists; the Grassmannian functor of locally free quotients of a module over an affine base is the only quotient-parameter functor, and it is not shown to be representable.

targets.target: Properness/projectivity of H -> S and Q -> S
targets.note: Proper morphisms, the valuative criterion and properness of Proj over Spec A_0 exist, but there is no parameter space to apply them to and no notion of projective morphism.

targets.target: Base-change compatibility of Hilbert and Quot schemes
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Flatness of the universal family U -> H and of the universal quotient (distinct from flatness of H -> S)
targets.note: Flat morphisms of schemes exist, but there are no universal families.

targets.target: Relative Hom schemes and Isom schemes
targets.note: No Hom or Isom functors of schemes over a base and no representability results for them exist.

targets.target: Dual-number degree-one Hilbert example proved by the rank-one quotient criterion
targets.note: The rank-one input is in Mathlib: a finite flat morphism is an isomorphism iff its rank is constantly 1, and a finite flat module over a local ring is free (which rules out flatness of k over k[ε]); Tau Ceti computes Ext^n over dual numbers. The degree-one Hilbert functor, its representation by X and the non-flatness of X -> S are not stated.

targets.target: Boundedness and realisation inside a Grassmannian (chart equations, universal quotient, flattening locus, gluing)
targets.note: Generic gluing tools exist (Zariski-local representability, relative gluing over locally directed covers, openness of the free locus of a finitely presented module), but there is no flattening stratification, generic flatness, Grassmannian chart or boundedness argument.

targets.target: Noetherian Chow lemma: proper surjective modification by a scheme quasi-projective over the base; projective dominating scheme over a field
targets.note: Proper morphisms and birational equivalence (isomorphic dense opens) exist; quasi-projective schemes and Chow's lemma do not.

targets.target: Coherent descent/dévissage statements for the selected proper-GAGA proof
targets.note: Finitely presented and quasi-coherent sheaves exist, but there is no coherent dévissage (filtrations with integral-subscheme quotients) and no GAGA-type statement.

duplicates.note: Constructs representable Hom functors (the finite locally free Weil-restriction case) and their base change, overlapping the relative Hom schemes of this layer.

targets.target: Étale equivalence relations and their quotients (algebraic spaces)
targets.note: Mathlib has internal equivalence relations in a category, the big étale topology and relatively representable morphisms; Tau Ceti has fppf quotient sheaves of affine groups by closed normal subgroups, with representability shown only for G/G^0 over an algebraically closed field. No algebraic spaces and no quotients of schemes by étale equivalence relations exist.

targets.target: Morphisms, fibre products and properties of algebraic spaces
targets.note: Only the presheaf-level transport of a scheme morphism property to representable morphisms exists (MorphismProperty.relative); nothing specific to algebraic spaces.

targets.target: Comparison with the finite étale quotient construction of #81
targets.note: Neither library contains the #81 quotient construction (no quotient of a scheme by a finite group, no modular-curve quotient); Mathlib only has the category of finite étale algebras.

targets.target: Effective descent for (quasi-coherent) sheaves
targets.note: Mathlib proves that extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic (affine faithfully flat descent for modules) and provides descent data, IsStack and the pseudofunctor of O_X-modules; Tau Ceti has Galois descent for semilinear representations. Missing: the stack property of quasi-coherent sheaves on schemes for fpqc/fppf/étale covers.

targets.target: Effective descent for finite flat group schemes
targets.note: Descent of morphisms is available: the fpqc topology is subcanonical (unnamed instance), faithfully flat surjections of affine schemes are regular epimorphisms, and points of an affine group scheme form an fppf sheaf. Missing: effectiveness of descent data for affine or finite locally free (group) schemes.

targets.target: Effective descent for polarisations and projective objects
targets.note: Mathlib descends properties of morphisms (isomorphism, open immersion, universally closed/open/injective, smooth, étale, finite presentation) along fpqc covers, but there is no descent of ample line bundles, polarisations or projective schemes.

targets.target: Descent of a line bundle kept separate from descent of an object equipped with that line bundle
targets.note: Invertible sheaves exist on a single scheme, but there is no descent statement for them or for pairs (object, line bundle).

targets.target: Weil restriction as an algebraic space for finite locally free bases (Stacks 05YC base-change map, 05YF representability)
targets.note: No Weil restriction (restriction of scalars) functor for schemes or algebraic spaces exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Also plans effective fpqc/fppf descent and algebraic-space quotients with representable diagonals.
Constructs quotients by finite locally free equivalence relations and free finite group actions, the scheme case of the equivalence-relation quotients here.
Proves effective faithfully flat descent for affine and finite locally free schemes, polarised projective curves, group objects and level structures, overlapping the effective-descent targets.
Owns Weil restriction of affine finite-type schemes along finite locally free maps, overlapping the Weil-restriction target in this layer's handoff.
Also constructs finite-locally-free Weil restriction for affine finitely presented schemes.

targets.target: Categories fibred in groupoids
targets.note: Mathlib has (pre)fibered categories in the sense of SGA 1 VI, the bicategory of based categories, fibre categories and the Grothendieck construction. Missing: the fibred-in-groupoids condition and its API (2-fibre products, 2-Yoneda).

targets.target: Stacks over a site: descent of morphisms and effectiveness of descent data
targets.note: The definitions exist for pseudofunctors LocallyDiscrete C^op -> Cat (fibres need not be groupoids), with a characterization via covering families of a precoverage. No comparison with fibered categories and no stack instances for schemes are proved.

targets.target: Stackification
targets.note: Only sheafification of presheaves exists; there is no stackification of prestacks or fibered categories.

targets.target: Representable diagonals
targets.note: Mathlib's criterion (diagonal relatively representable iff all maps from representables are) covers set-valued presheaves, i.e. the algebraic-space case. Missing: representability of the diagonal for stacks via Isom sheaves.

targets.target: Smooth/étale atlases and algebraic (Artin, Deligne-Mumford) stacks
targets.note: Smooth and étale morphisms of schemes and the étale topologies exist; there are no atlases and no algebraic stacks.

targets.target: Quotient stacks and their algebraicity
targets.note: There are no group actions on schemes, quotient stacks or stacks of torsors; Tau Ceti's fppf quotient sheaves of affine groups by normal subgroups are the closest construction.

targets.target: Algebraicity of moduli stacks of generalised elliptic curves and polarised abelian schemes
targets.note: Only abelian varieties over a field (Tau Ceti) and Weierstrass curves (Mathlib) exist; generalised elliptic curves, abelian schemes over a base, polarisations and their moduli stacks do not.

targets.target: Deligne-Mumford, separated, proper and tame properties of stacks with distinct proofs
targets.note: Only the scheme versions of separated and proper exist; there are no Deligne-Mumford or tameness conditions.

duplicates.note: Also plans stacks with representable diagonals and atlas independence.
Also plans groupoid-valued prestacks, descent data, stackification and quotients of groupoids on general sites.
Defines the category fibred in groupoids Ell/R of elliptic curves, a special case of the fibred-category target.

targets.target: Existence of coarse spaces for the finite-inertia/quotient presentations used
targets.note: Mathlib shows a ring is integral over its invariants under a finite group and that the group acts transitively on the primes over a given prime (the ring-level input for Spec(B)/G). There are no coarse moduli spaces, Keel-Mori theorem or quotient schemes.

targets.target: Base-change statements for coarse spaces
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Adding or removing auxiliary prime-to-characteristic level and rigidification of automorphisms
targets.note: Tau Ceti computes Aut(E) = {±1} for a Weierstrass curve over a field with j not 0 or 1728; there are no level structures, no Serre rigidity lemma and no rigidified moduli problems.

targets.target: Normalisation
targets.note: Relative normalization of Y in X for a qcqs morphism X -> Y, with the universal property among integral factorizations, compatibility with coproducts and (unnamed IsIso instance, Stacks 03GV) smooth base change. Finiteness of the normalization is not included (see A0-extension).

targets.target: Schematic closure (scheme-theoretic image)
targets.note: Scheme-theoretic image as the closed subscheme of the kernel ideal sheaf, the factorization through it and the kernel/subscheme adjunction (full names AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.image, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toImage, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.kerAdjunction; declarations.tsv records the short names). Flat base change is only shown for quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dominant morphisms.

targets.target: Descent of finite correspondences
targets.note: No correspondences on schemes (e.g. Hecke correspondences) and no descent statements for them exist.

targets.target: Required examples: finite constant-group quotient in tame characteristic and a non-tame example
targets.note: Only ring-level invariant theory exists; there are no quotient schemes by finite constant groups and no tameness notion.

targets.target: Required example: the coarse j-line and the moduli stack of elliptic curves are not interchangeable
targets.note: Mathlib shows that over a separably closed field curves with equal j are isomorphic and every j occurs, and Tau Ceti computes generic automorphism groups; neither the j-line as a coarse space nor the stack of elliptic curves exists.

duplicates.note: Constructs coarse moduli schemes as finite quotients of rigidified moduli with base-change statements (KM 8.1), overlapping coarse spaces for finite quotient presentations.
Constructs auxiliary rigidifying level structures and the resulting finite étale equivalence relations, overlapping rigidification by auxiliary level.
Constructs coarse compactified modular curves by finite-inertia quotients and normalization, a specialisation of the coarse-space target.
Restates that a sufficiently rigidifying prime-to-p level eliminates automorphisms.
Also asks to separate a coarse space from a fine moduli object and to supply quotient universal properties.

targets.target: Deformation functor at a geometric point and its identification with the completed local ring
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Zariski tangent spaces and the dual-number/derivation dictionary, and Mathlib lifts maps out of formally smooth algebras along adically complete quotients (exists_mkₐ_comp_eq_of_isAdicComplete, not in declarations.tsv: public modifier). There are no deformation functors on Artinian local algebras, no Schlessinger criterion, no pro-representability and no completed local rings of schemes.

targets.target: Stabilisers, versal groupoids and versality
targets.note: No versal deformations, deformation groupoids or stabiliser comparisons exist.

targets.target: Algebraisation statements (effectivity, Grothendieck existence) needed by R10/R13
targets.note: There are no formal schemes, no formal GAGA or Grothendieck existence theorem, and no effectivity results.

targets.target: Named universal properties exported for every consumed parameter space
targets.note: None of the roadmap's parameter spaces exist, so no universal properties can be exported; affine space's universal property is the only representing-object statement of this kind in Mathlib.

targets.target: Artin representability with its hypotheses and a proof
targets.note: As in A0-extension, only generic inputs exist (limit preservation of functors of points of locally finitely presented schemes, the representable-diagonal criterion for presheaves); the theorem itself is absent.

duplicates.note: Also plans infinitesimal lifting, obstruction theory, formal schemes and algebraization with comparison to completions.
Constructs universal deformations of elliptic curves and compares them with completed local rings of representing moduli schemes, a special case.
Also proves Schlessinger's pro-representability criterion, the general criterion behind the deformation-functor comparison.
Owns formal functions and formal GAGA in the proper finite-presentation setting, the algebraization input this layer restates.

targets.target: Embedded resolution of singularities for varieties over a characteristic-zero field by blowing up (Bierstone-Milman Theorem 11.14)
targets.note: Neither library has blowups, normal-crossings divisors or any resolution theorem; only regular local rings, smooth morphisms and the Rees algebra exist (see R09.7a-c).

targets.target: Preservation of already-resolved (regular/SNC) points (Bierstone-Milman Theorem 12.2)
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Global construction compatible with local isomorphisms (Bierstone-Milman Theorem 13.2)
targets.note: Nothing exists; no functoriality statement for resolution under étale or smooth morphisms.

targets.target: Smooth projective compactification with simple normal-crossings boundary (exported through R09.7d)
targets.note: No projective morphisms, compactifications or SNC divisors exist.

duplicates.note: Also constructs Rees-algebra blowups with universal property, strict transforms and affine charts (the R09.7a part), though its resolution theorem is for arithmetic surfaces, not characteristic zero.
Also plans flattening by blowup, strict transforms and compactification of pairs, but for de Jong alterations rather than resolution.

targets.target: Blowups via the Rees algebra with projective universal property and affine charts
targets.note: Mathlib's Rees algebra R[It] (a subalgebra of R[X], of finite type for finitely generated I, without a graded-ring instance) and Proj with basic-open affine charts exist, but there is no blowup scheme, exceptional divisor or universal property; the Rees algebra docstring lists blowups as future work.

targets.target: Strict, total and controlled transforms of ideals and subschemes
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Smooth base-change comparison for blowups
targets.note: Nothing exists (no blowups).

targets.target: Simple normal-crossings boundary divisors and permissible smooth centres transverse to the accumulated boundary
targets.note: Cartier divisors on integral schemes (Tau Ceti), regular local rings and smooth morphisms (Mathlib) exist; there are no regular parameter systems adapted to divisors, SNC divisors or permissible centres.

targets.target: Marked ideals and their equivalence under admissible transformations
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Local order and exceptional-multiplicity calculations
targets.note: Only the order of vanishing of a rational function at a codimension-one point exists; there is no order of an ideal at a point and no multiplicity along exceptional divisors.

duplicates.note: Constructs the Rees algebra and blowup of a quasi-coherent finite-type ideal as relative Proj with universal property, exceptional divisor, strict transform and affine charts: the same blowup package.
Also lists flattening by blowup and strict transforms as internal tasks.

targets.target: Order/multiplicity invariant on smooth characteristic-zero charts
targets.note: Only codimension-one orders of rational functions exist; no ideal order or multiplicity invariant.

targets.target: Maximal-contact hypersurfaces in characteristic zero
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Coefficient ideals and inductive dimension reduction
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Independence of equivalent presentations, upper semicontinuity and compatibility with smooth coordinate changes
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Exceptional-divisor history and the monomial case
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Permissible globally compatible centres from the maximum loci of the full invariant
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Decrease of the complete invariant and termination, including residual monomial clean-up
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Principalization (invertible total transform with normal-crossings support) and embedded desingularization
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Isomorphism over the prescribed regular/SNC locus and the functoriality provided by the source
targets.note: Nothing exists.

targets.target: Projective closure of a smooth quasi-projective variety over a characteristic-zero field
targets.note: There are no quasi-projective varieties or projective embeddings; only Proj of graded rings and general scheme-theoretic images exist.

targets.target: Smooth projective compactification with strict normal-crossings complement preserving the given smooth open
targets.note: Proper and smooth morphisms exist; compactifications and SNC complements do not.

targets.target: Analytic polydisc charts along the boundary over the complex numbers
targets.note: No complex analytification of schemes exists; Tau Ceti's polydiscs are adic (valuation-spectrum) objects, unrelated to this target.

duplicates.note: Also constructs a smooth projective compactification of nonproper smooth curves (the dimension-one case) for its logarithmic de Rham comparison.
Also constructs smooth projective completions of smooth affine complex curves by projective closure and normalization (the dimension-one case).

SchemeAndStackFoundations.summary: Mathlib already contains most of SF.0 (schemes, quasi-coherent modules with the tilde equivalence, gluing, fibre products, and flat/smooth/étale/proper/separated/finite-presentation morphisms with their base-change laws) and much of the framework behind SF.1–SF.2 (fppf, fpqc, étale and pro-étale topologies, fpqc descent of morphism properties, abstract descent data and IsStack, sheaf cohomology on sites, pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology), together with rational maps and algebraic cycles with pushforward; Tau Ceti adds cohomology of O_X-modules, Weil/Cartier divisors and line bundles on curves, models over DVRs, and the complete function-field Riemann–Roch theory with genus that SF.3 asks to integrate. Genuinely missing: relative Spec/Proj of quasi-coherent algebras over a general base, effective descent of quasi-coherent sheaves, algebraic spaces, algebraic stacks and coarse/fine moduli, étale localization, proper/smooth base change and compact support, sheaf-theoretic Riemann–Roch and Serre duality, Picard schemes, Jacobians and Tate modules, formal schemes, algebraization, Néron models, alterations and semistable reduction, and all intersection theory beyond cycles and pushforward (Chow groups, Chern classes, Gysin maps, Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch, Hodge index). SF.3 and SF.6 largely restate or integrate other owners (AlgebraicCurves, JacobianChallenge, CohomologyComparisons), and the inputs of SF.0–SF.1 point to the retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration roadmap, whose material is in Mathlib.

targets.target: Schemes, Spec and affine schemes
targets.note: Mathlib defines schemes as locally ringed spaces locally isomorphic to Spec, with morphisms, the Spec functor and affine schemes; nothing to build.

targets.target: Sheaves of O_X-modules and quasi-coherence (M~ equivalence on affines, pullback/pushforward)
targets.note: Mathlib has the abelian category X.Modules, quasi-coherence (defined for sheaves of modules on any ringed site via local presentations), and ModuleCat R equivalent to quasi-coherent O_{Spec R}-modules. Tau Ceti adds the tensor product of O_X-modules (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorProduct) and finitely presented sheaves, which the layer does not ask for.

targets.target: Relative Spec of a quasi-coherent O_S-algebra
targets.note: Mathlib glues Spec of a 'coequifibered' presheaf of O_X-algebras on the affine Zariski site (F(D(f)) = F(U)[1/f]) into a scheme over X, and has relative Spec over an affine base (algSpec: R-algebras to schemes over Spec R); relative normalization is built this way. Missing: a named Spec functor on quasi-coherent O_S-algebras and its anti-equivalence with affine morphisms to S (Mathlib's docstring says the link to quasi-coherent algebras is still to be developed).

targets.target: Relative Proj of a graded quasi-coherent O_S-algebra
targets.note: Mathlib has Proj of an N-graded ring as a scheme over Spec A_0, with its standard affine cover, and proves Proj A -> Spec A_0 is separated, and proper when A is of finite type over A_0 (an unnamed instance in ProjectiveSpectrum/Proper.lean). Missing: Proj of a graded quasi-coherent algebra over a general base scheme, with O(1) and base change.

targets.target: Gluing schemes along open subschemes (affine gluing)
targets.note: Mathlib glues arbitrary gluing data of schemes (not only affine pieces), with open immersions and joint surjectivity, shows a scheme is the colimit of its affine opens, and has relative gluing over a locally directed open cover of the base (Stacks 01LH).

targets.target: Fibre products of schemes
targets.note: Mathlib builds fibre products by gluing from the affine case (Spec S x_{Spec R} Spec T = Spec (S tensor_R T)); the global HasPullbacks Scheme instance is unnamed (Pullbacks.lean line 484) so it is not in the declaration list.

targets.target: Flat, smooth and etale morphisms as named morphism properties
targets.note: Defined affine-locally (flat/smooth/etale ring maps on affine opens), with stalk characterisations and Etale iff smooth of relative dimension 0 (AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.iff_smoothOfRelativeDimension_zero).

targets.target: Proper, separated and locally-of-finite-presentation morphisms as named morphism properties
targets.note: IsProper is separated + universally closed + locally of finite type; IsSeparated means the diagonal is a closed immersion. Valuative criteria are also in Mathlib (ValuativeCriterion.lean).

targets.target: Base-change and composition stability of these properties (base-change squares)
targets.note: All are MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange instances (also IsSeparated.isStableUnderBaseChange, composition instances). The acceptance remark that a flat family does not make its parameter scheme flat is a warning, not a theorem to formalise.

duplicates.note: Also plans relative Proj of a finitely generated graded quasi-coherent algebra and projective morphisms.
Its projective bundles are the relative Proj construction of this layer.

targets.target: fpqc and fppf topologies on schemes, subcanonical (descent of morphisms into a scheme)
targets.note: Mathlib defines the fppf and fpqc topologies on Sch and proves them subcanonical, so quasi-compact (or locally finitely presented) faithfully flat surjections are effective epimorphisms; these instances are unnamed in Sites/Fpqc.lean. Tau Ceti adds the induced fppf topology on affine R-schemes (CommAlgCat R)^op with subcanonicity.

targets.target: fpqc descent of properties of morphisms
targets.note: Isomorphisms, open immersions, surjective, universally closed/open/injective, flat, and (unnamed instances in LocalFlatDescent.lean) locally of finite type/presentation, smooth, formally unramified and etale all descend along surjective flat quasi-compact morphisms. Mathlib's Descent.lean lists descent of affine morphisms along faithfully flat maps as TODO.

targets.target: Effective fpqc/fppf descent of objects (quasi-coherent modules, affine schemes)
targets.note: Mathlib proves extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic (affine faithfully flat descent of modules in Beck form) and the Amitsur exactness R -> S => S (x)_R S; Tau Ceti proves the affine group-valued points descend. Missing: the stack statement that quasi-coherent sheaves (or affine morphisms) satisfy effective fpqc/fppf descent over schemes; Mathlib's ModuleCat/Descent.lean marks the passage to effective descent as TODO.

targets.target: Descent data, prestacks and stacks over a site (fibered categories)

targets.target: Riemann-Roch theorem for curves (function-field form)
targets.note: Proved for an algebraic function field F/k with exact constant field (IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F): l(D) = deg D + 1 - g + l(W - D) with W the divisor of a Weil differential, deg W = 2g - 2, and the high-degree form. Stated for function fields, not for curves as schemes.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves.summary: Tau Ceti already contains nearly all of Stichtenoth Chapter I, with exact constants assumed only where the source needs them: intrinsic function fields and constant fields, normalized places with degrees, weak and strong approximation, the classification of the places of k(x), divisors with the product formula, L(D), the genus and Riemann's theorem, repartitions and Weil differentials, the canonical class and the Riemann–Roch theorem with its uniqueness (Layers 1 and 4 are fully built), the high-degree regime, the genus-0 criterion, Weierstrass gaps and finiteness of Cl⁰. It also has most of III.1–III.3 and III.7 (extensions of places, conorm, geometric degree, the fundamental identity for separable extensions, both halves of Kummer's theorem, the Galois action, decomposition/inertia groups and lower ramification groups, the different divisor with the tame value d = e − 1) and the elliptic dictionary W.Point ≃+ Cl⁰ with W.CoordinateRing Dedekind, so the roadmap's summary and README treat much built work as missing. Genuinely missing: infinitude of places, general finite normalization and two-chart compatibility, Clifford's theorem, the cotrace and the Hurwitz genus formula together with everything resting on it (the genus of Weierstrass, hyperelliptic, plane, Kummer and Artin–Schreier curves), constant-field extensions and genus invariance, Hilbert's different formula, Abhyankar's lemma and the inseparable genus bounds, local expansions, residues and the Kähler–Weil comparison, the automorphism layer (Aut(k(x)) ≅ PGL₂, rigidity, Weierstrass points, the 84(g − 1) bound), and the whole scheme-side dictionary of Layer 12 (ℙ¹_k, projective morphisms, the regular projective model, the anti-equivalence, H⁰ = L(D) and the cohomological genus).

targets.note: Mathlib's Lüroth: every intermediate field E of K(X)/K equals K⟮generator E⟯, and for E ≠ ⊥ there is K⟮X⟯ ≃ₐ[K] E; RatFunc.Luroth.eq_adjoin_generator and RatFunc.Luroth.algEquiv (not in declarations.tsv: public modifier). targets.target: k[X] is Japanese/Nagata (or its one-dimensional special case)
targets.note: Neither library has an IsJapanese/IsNagata/N-2 notion; Tau Ceti's DedekindDomain/IntegralClosure docstring records that a normalization-finiteness theorem of Nagata type is not available. Only the separable and purely inseparable special cases below exist.

targets.target: normalization of k[X] in every finite extension of k(X) is a finite k[X]-module, no separability
targets.note: Present: the separable case (Mathlib, trace form; Tau Ceti's polynomial-model form) and the purely inseparable case for k[X_1..X_r] (Stacks 032O). Missing: the general mixed-separability statement (e.g. via normal closure and the purely inseparable subextension), which nobody has assembled; Krull–Akizuki gives Noetherianity only, not module-finiteness.

targets.target: R_x Noetherian, integrally closed, Krull dimension ≤ 1, fraction field F (no separability)
targets.note: Integral closedness, dimension ≤ 1 and the fraction field are separability-free Mathlib results; Noetherianity without separability is Tau Ceti's Krull–Akizuki theorem (any Noetherian domain of dimension ≤ 1, any finite extension of its fraction field), not a consequence of finite normalization as the layer prescribes (module-finiteness is not obtained).

targets.target: hence R_x is a Dedekind domain (no separability)
targets.note: Tau Ceti: the integral closure of any Dedekind domain A in any finite extension L of Frac A is Dedekind, no separability; this covers R_x (A = k[x], L = F) but no R_x-specific statement is packaged. Mathlib's criterion (Noetherian + DVR localizations; not in declarations.tsv: public modifier) is the alternative route through the places ↔ primes dictionary.

targets.target: separable branch via IsIntegralClosure.isDedekindDomain and integralClosure.isFractionRing_of_finite_extension
targets.note: Both named Mathlib results exist; the Dedekind ones carry [Algebra.IsSeparable K L], the fraction-field lemma does not.

targets.target: ord_P(x) ≥ 0 ↔ k[x] ⊆ 𝒪_P; integrality then gives R_x ⊆ 𝒪_P
targets.note: Stated with x ∈ 𝒪_P (Algebra.adjoin k {x} ⊆ 𝒪_P ↔ x ∈ 𝒪_P); the additive ord form is mem_integers_iff_ord_nonneg.

targets.target: contraction to a height-one prime 𝔭_P, (R_x)_{𝔭_P} ≃ 𝒪_P, normalized adic valuation equals P.valuation exactly
targets.note: For any Dedekind k-algebra R with IsFractionRing R F contained in 𝒪_P: valuation of the centre = P.valuation (equality), and Mathlib's localization-at-prime valuation subring equals 𝒪_P as subrings of F (stronger than a ring isomorphism).

targets.target: converse (place of a height-one prime), mutual inverses, bijection {P | ord_P x ≥ 0} ≃ HeightOneSpectrum R_x
targets.note: The bijection is {P // R ⊆ 𝒪_P} ≃ HeightOneSpectrum R for any Dedekind model R; the R_x instance with index set {P | ord_P x ≥ 0} is not packaged but follows from adjoin_le_integers_iff and mem_integers_of_isIntegral_adjoin.

targets.target: induced residue-field equivalence, equality of residue degrees, ord_P/intValuation coefficient formula
targets.note: R ⧸ 𝔭 ≃ₐ[k] F_P, deg P = [R ⧸ 𝔭 : k], v_P(r) = intValuation 𝔭 r, and ord_P r = multiplicity of 𝔭 in (r) for r ≠ 0; again for an arbitrary Dedekind model.

targets.target: two-chart compatibility: R_x and R_{x⁻¹} agree on the common localization with equal normalized valuations
targets.note: No statement relates the charts of x and x⁻¹ or their overlap localization. Each chart separately is fine (valuations are equal to place valuations, hence automatically compatible), but the gluing is not formalized; Tau Ceti's extension/different files use a second-model hypothesis or the local models over 𝒪_P instead.

targets.target: places with ord_P x < 0 = finite-chart primes of x⁻¹ = places over P_∞; their finiteness
targets.note: Finiteness of the poles of x is proved (via Prop. 1.3.3, not via finite normalization), and the complement of a chart is characterized; missing is the explicit identification of these places with the height-one primes of R_{x⁻¹} and with the places of F lying over P_∞ of k(x).

targets.target: S-domains / holomorphy rings 𝒪_S (Stichtenoth III.2), via Set.integer
targets.note: Built directly for any set of places (integrally closed, fraction field F if S misses a place, every integrally closed k-subalgebra is some 𝒪_S so R_x = 𝒪_{ord_P x ≥ 0}, PID and S ≃ HeightOneSpectrum 𝒪_S for finite S), deliberately not through Mathlib's Set.integer and with no bridge to it; Dedekindness for infinite proper S is not stated.

duplicates.note: Also identifies affine places with maximal ideals of the coordinate ring and asks for the coordinate ring to be Dedekind (the elliptic special case).
Also constructs the normalization of a projective model of a function field.

targets.target: Divisor group Place →₀ ℤ, degree hom, order, ⊔/⊓, positive/negative parts (Def. 1.4.1)

targets.target: Finiteness of zeros and poles via ∑ ord·deg ≤ [F : k(f)] (Prop. 1.3.3, Cor. 1.3.4)
targets.note: Stated for every x : F (the set is empty at the junk value x = 0); the weighted bound needs only FiniteDimensional k⟮x⟯ F, no exact-constants hypothesis.

targets.target: Principal divisor hom div : Fˣ → Divisor k F, zero and pole divisors (Def. 1.4.2)
targets.note: principalHom : Additive Fˣ →+ Divisor k F via the WeilDivisor.OrderSystem of places (hF explicit); zeros = (div z)⁺ and poles = (div z)⁻.

targets.target: div f = 0 iff f ∈ kˣ over an exact constant field
targets.note: principal_eq_zero_iff assumes IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F; without it the kernel is identified with algebraicClosure k F.

targets.target: Product formula: deg (f)₀ = deg (f)_∞ = [F : k(f)] and deg div f = 0 (Thm. 1.4.11)
targets.note: The degree formulas assume f transcendental over k (equivalent to nonconstant when constants are exact) and need no exactness; degree_principal holds for every f ∈ Fˣ.

targets.target: Cl(F), Cl⁰(F) and the degree exact sequence 0 → Cl⁰ → Cl → deg-image → 0 (Def. 1.4.3)
targets.note: Cl(F) = (Place.orderSystem hF).ClassGroup and Cl⁰ = ker degreeClass; Cl/Cl⁰ ≃ range of degree and (ker deg)/principal ≃ Cl⁰ are proved for any order system with degree-zero principal divisors (satisfied via Place.isWeightedDegreeZero_orderSystem), but are not restated under function-field names.

targets.target: Linear equivalence preserves deg and ℓ (Cor. 1.4.12(a))
targets.note: Both need only IsFunctionField k F.

targets.target: Degree-zero divisor principal iff ℓ ≥ 1 iff ℓ = 1 (Cor. 1.4.12(c))
targets.note: The ℓ = 1 form assumes IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F; the ℓ ≥ 1 form and the general ℓ = [k̃ : k] form need only hF.

targets.target: Riemann–Roch space L(D) : Submodule k F and ℓ(D) (Def. 1.4.4, Rem. 1.4.5, Def. 1.4.10)
targets.note: Carrier is the pinned multiplicative condition v_P f ≤ exp (D P); ℓ(D) := Module.finrank k (L D).

targets.target: L(A) ≅ L(A′) for linearly equivalent divisors (Lemma 1.4.6)
targets.note: k-linear isomorphism L(A) ≃ L(A − div z) given by multiplication by z.

targets.target: L(0) = k and L(D) = 0 when D < 0 or deg D < 0 (Lemma 1.4.7, Cor. 1.4.12(b))
targets.note: L(0) = k needs IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F (in general L(0) = algebraicClosure k F); the vanishing statements need only hF.

targets.target: Monotonicity and dim L(D′)/L(D) ≤ deg D′ − deg D (Lemma 1.4.8)
targets.note: Includes the one-place estimate ℓ(D + P) ≤ ℓ(D) + deg P; no exactness hypothesis.

targets.target: Finite-dimensionality of L(D) with ℓ(D) ≤ deg D⁺ + 1 (Prop. 1.4.9)
targets.note: Finiteness needs only hF; the +1 bound assumes IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F (general bound has +[k̃ : k]).

targets.target: deg D − ℓ(D) is bounded above (Prop. 1.4.14)
targets.note: No hypothesis on the constant field.

targets.target: Genus g = sSup {deg A − ℓ(A) + 1} and g ≥ 0 / attained (Def. 1.4.15, Cor. 1.4.16)

targets.target: Riemann's theorem ℓ(D) ≥ deg D + 1 − g, with equality for deg D ≥ c (Thm. 1.4.17)
targets.note: The inequality needs only hF; the ∃ c equality form assumes IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F.

targets.target: Index of specialty i(D) = ℓ(D) − deg D − 1 + g ≥ 0, vanishing in large degree (Def. 1.5.1)
targets.note: Vanishing in large degree assumes IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F.

targets.target: k(x): div x = P_(X) − P_∞
targets.note: All coefficientwise ingredients exist (ord_∞ f = −intDegree f, ord of X at each finite place, classification of places of k(x)), but the divisor identity div x = P_(X) − P_∞ is not stated.

targets.target: k(x): deg (f)_∞ = max(natDegree num, natDegree denom) = [k(x) : k(f)]
targets.note: Both halves exist (Tau Ceti: deg (f)_∞ = [F : k(f)] for transcendental f; Mathlib: [k(X) : k(f)] = max of the natDegrees); only their composite for RatFunc k is not stated.

targets.target: k(x): ∑_p natDegree p · ord_p f = intDegree f (product formula on ℙ¹, concretely)
targets.note: Follows from the general product formula with deg P_q = natDegree q, deg P_∞ = 1 and ord_∞ f = −intDegree f, but the explicit sum over monic irreducibles is not stated.

targets.target: k(x): L(n·P_∞) = polynomials of degree ≤ n, ℓ(n·P_∞) = n + 1
targets.note: Over an arbitrary field k, computed by hand without Riemann–Roch; also (n + 1)⁺ for every integer n.

targets.target: g(k(x)) = 0 and Riemann's inequality sharp (Ex. 1.4.18)
targets.note: Over any field k; dim_ratFunc gives ℓ(D) = (deg D + 1)⁺ for every divisor of k(x).

targets.target: Affine bridge: finite-chart divisors ≅ (FractionalIdeal R⁰ F)ˣ via FractionalIdeal.count
targets.note: For any Dedekind model R with fraction field F (R_x qualifies without separability by TauCeti.IsIntegralClosure.isDedekindDomain). targets.target: Cl⁰(F) ≅ ClassGroup R for a model with a single degree-1 place at infinity
targets.note: Hypotheses: the set of places infinite on R is {P} and deg P = 1 (surjectivity alone needs only some rational place at infinity); not yet instantiated at Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve (Layer 10).

targets.note: Submodule k (Place k F → F) cut out by ∀ᶠ P in cofinite, v_P (a P) ≤ 1 — no completions, exactly as pinned; closed under multiplication and F-scaling.

targets.target: Diagonal embedding F ↪ A_F
targets.note: The diagonal is the image of Pi.constAlgHom; landing in A_F uses finiteness of zeros/poles (needs hF).

targets.target: Filtration A_F(D) in multiplicative junk-free form and its calculus: 0 ∈ A_F(D), k-submodule, monotone, A_F(D) + F ≤ A_F, A_F = ⋃ A_F(D) (Def. 1.5.3)

targets.target: Local quotient dim_k (𝔪_P^a / 𝔪_P^b) = (b − a)·deg P
targets.note: 𝔪_P^a is realized inside F for every integer a (v_P z ≤ exp (−a)); the rank version needs no finiteness of the residue field.

targets.target: A_F(E)/A_F(D) ≅ ⊕_{supp(E−D)} local quotients; finite-dimensional of dimension deg E − deg D
targets.note: The equivalence holds for any finite set of places containing supp (E − D); the dimension count assumes D ≤ E and hF.

targets.target: i(D) = dim_k A_F ⧸ (A_F(D) + F) (Thm. 1.5.4) and g = dim_k A_F ⧸ (A_F(0) + F) (Cor. 1.5.5)
targets.note: Hypotheses hF and IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F; also A_F(D) + F = A_F iff i(D) = 0.

targets.target: Weil differentials Ω_F, Ω_F(A), dim_k Ω_F(A) = i(A) and Ω_F ≠ 0 (Def. 1.5.6, Lemma 1.5.7)

targets.note: (f·ω)(a) = ω(f·a); the Module F instance is a def introduced with letI because hF is an explicit hypothesis.

targets.target: dim_F Ω_F = 1 (Prop. 1.5.9)
targets.note: Hypotheses hF and IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F.

targets.note: canonicalClass hF hex : (Place.orderSystem hF).ClassGroup; every nonzero Weil differential represents it.

targets.note: k-linear equivalence x ↦ x·ω for W the greatest divisor bounding ω ≠ 0; hypotheses hF and IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F.

targets.note: IsRiemannRochDivisor W g₀ is the identity for all D; proved for W = (ω) and for every divisor of the canonical class, with only IsFunctionField k F and IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F (no perfectness or separability).

targets.target: ℓ(W) = g and deg W = 2g − 2 (Cor. 1.5.16)
targets.note: Stated for (ω), for the canonical class, and for any Riemann–Roch divisor; exact constants assumed.

targets.target: Characterization of canonical divisors: deg D = 2g − 2 and ℓ(D) ≥ g ⟹ D canonical (Prop. 1.6.2)

targets.target: Genus-one ladder ℓ(n·[0]) = n for n ≥ 1 at a rational place

targets.target: Strong approximation for proper S ⊊ ℙ_F (Thm. 1.6.5)
targets.note: Hypotheses hF, IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F, S ≠ univ and a finite s ⊆ S with targets and orders; exact orders at s and integrality at S \ s.

targets.note: Hypotheses hF and IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F for the nonvanishing and order statements.

targets.target: intrinsic characterization ∃ A, deg A = 2 ∧ ℓ(A) ≥ 2, and every genus-2 function field over perfect k is hyperelliptic (Lemma 6.2.2)
targets.note: Not found.

targets.target: uniqueness of the degree-2 rational subfield ([F : k(z)] ≤ g ⟹ k(z) ⊆ k(x)) and its description by regular differentials (Prop. 6.2.4)
targets.note: Not found.

targets.target: projective plane curves: homogeneous coordinates, three affine charts, smoothness via homogeneous partials, function field of an integral plane equation

targets.note: Mathlib only records 2-pretransitivity of GL on a projectivization. No sharp 3-transitivity or fixed-point rigidity for PGL₂ was found.

targets.target: finiteness of Aut(F/k̄) for g ≥ 2 over algebraically closed char-0 k (non-hyperelliptic and hyperelliptic cases)
targets.note: Not found. The prerequisites (rigidity, Weierstrass-point counts, Prop. 6.2.4, PGL₂ rigidity) are also absent.

targets.note: Not found. Riemann–Hurwitz for F/F^G is also absent from the baseline.

targets.note: No Hermitian function field or its automorphisms in either library.

Tau Ceti packages it as an additive hom on k(X)ˣ and proves it surjective when the stalk is a DVR. On a 1-dimensional integral scheme the codimension-one points are the non-generic points.

targets.note: No construction of a TauCeti.Place from a scheme point, and no finiteness or transcendence-degree statement for X.functionField. Tau Ceti has the 1-dimensional Hartogs lemma for DVR stalks, a related local input.

targets.note: Mathlib has relative normalization of a qcqs morphism, universal among integral factorizations, which could express 'normalize ℙ¹_k in F'. But neither library has ℙ¹_k (or ℙⁿ) as a scheme, and finiteness of the normalization is also absent.

targets.note: No projective-morphism predicate was found in Mathlib or Tau Ceti AlgebraicGeometry.

targets.note: Mathlib identifies S-morphisms Spec K(X) → Y with S-rational maps X ⇢ Y (Y locally of finite type, X integral). No extension of rational maps from regular curves, and no curve category or anti-equivalence.

targets.target: 12C acceptance: for W.FunctionField, isogenies ↔ scheme morphisms, with the place at O₁ restricting to the place at O₂
targets.note: Tau Ceti isogenies are coordinate-ring/function-field pullbacks sending infinity to infinity. There is no scheme-morphism side to compare them with.

targets.target: 12D: Weil divisors on a scheme (free abelian group on codimension-one points), principal divisors, linear equivalence, residue-degree-weighted degree, stated against Mathlib's cycle vocabulary
targets.note: Built for arbitrary schemes, with principal divisors for [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X] and the bridge to Mathlib's AlgebraicCycle. It is the JacobianChallenge Layer A development, not a model X_F. The class group is WeilDivisor.OrderSystem.ClassGroup of ofScheme.

targets.note: Only the function-field ladder ℓ(n·P) = n (rational P, genus 1, exact constants) exists. The scheme-side statement is absent.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AnalyticToricGeom.summary: Tau Ceti already builds most of Layer 0's combinatorics (integral lattices, toric cones on Mathlib PointedCones, rays with unique primitive generators, regular cones with the extending-basis block form, finite fans, subfans, products, subdivisions and fan morphisms) and much of the analytic calculus of Layers 1–2 (a coordinate-free complex torus with characters, maps on affine complex points, mixed monomial maps with composition on the torus locus and unimodular biholomorphisms, and the monomial-embedding topology, which is Hausdorff, locally compact and second countable). Genuinely missing: intersections of arbitrary toric cones and generation by rays (Mathlib has no Minkowski–Weyl theorem), simpliciality of regular cones, dual semigroups and Gordan's lemma, every scheme-level toric object (affine toric schemes, face localizations as open immersions, fan gluing, torus actions), and everything analytic from the regular charts onward (manifold charts, gluing, orbits and boundary, toric maps and properness, the global comparison). The external Toric project's ToricVariety, which the document treats as an existing foundation, is in neither library, while Mathlib's Spec.homEquivAlgHom already gives the pointwise bijection of Layer 6 for any affine scheme.

targets.target: Integral-lattice predicate via an R-linear equivalence R tensor N = N_R restricting to i
targets.note: IsIntegralLattice packages Module.Free and Module.Finite over Z with Mathlib's IsBaseChange R for i; isIntegralLattice_iff restates it as an R-linear equivalence sending 1 tensor n to i n. Sorry-free.

targets.target: Injectivity, discreteness, spanning and equality of integral and real ranks of an integral lattice
targets.note: Discreteness is stated for a normed real space V: the range is discrete and is an IsZLattice. finiteDimensional is also proved.

targets.target: Naturality of integral lattices under integral linear maps
targets.note: A map of integral vectors extends uniquely to an R-linear map (extend, eq_extend, extend_id, extend_comp); being a lattice transfers along compatible equivalences and to products.

targets.target: IsToricCone on a Mathlib PointedCone: finite generation, lattice rationality, salience
targets.note: Structure with fields rational and salient (ConvexCone.Salient); finite generation is derived from rationality (IsToricCone.fg) rather than being a field. Only AddCommGroup N is assumed.

targets.target: Toric cones preserved by faces, products, injective integral maps and lattice equivalences
targets.note: IsToricCone.map needs an injective R-linear map compatible with an additive map of lattices; the equivalence version is an iff.

targets.target: Toric cones preserved under intersections
targets.note: Only intersections inside a fan are covered (they are faces by the fan axiom, hence toric). Missing: the intersection of two arbitrary toric cones for an integral lattice is toric; this needs Minkowski-Weyl (FG iff DualFG), which Mathlib mentions only in a docstring. Counterexamples.lean shows failure for a non-lattice map.

targets.target: Rays as one-dimensional Mathlib faces; finiteness of the ray type
targets.note: ToricRay is the subtype of PointedCone.Face with one-dimensional span; finiteness needs only finite generation of the cone. Rays of products and faces are also handled (prodSplit, faceEmbedding).

targets.target: Existence and uniqueness of the primitive generator of every ray
targets.note: Requires IsIntegralLattice i and a toric ray (primitiveGenerator takes a toric ambient cone and uses its face). Primitivity is TauCeti.IsPrimitive (some Z-functional takes the value 1).

targets.target: Naturality of rays and primitive generators under lattice equivalences
targets.note: Stated for a compatible pair of an additive equivalence of lattices and an R-linear equivalence; identity and composition laws hold up to a cast of the image cone.

targets.target: Generation of a toric cone by its primitive ray generators
targets.note: No theorem, in Mathlib or Tau Ceti, that a salient finitely generated cone is the hull of its rays or of its primitive ray generators; Mathlib's Krein-Milman is for compact convex sets.

targets.target: Regularity: IsToricCone plus an integral basis containing every primitive ray generator
targets.note: IsRegularCone extends IsToricCone with an integral basis indexed by Fin n and an injection of the rays into its indices whose basis vectors are the primitive generators.

targets.target: Regular cones are simplicial
targets.note: Mathlib defines PointedCone.IsSimplicial, but no theorem says regular cones are simplicial; Regular.lean says simpliciality 'is not proved here' and only bounds the number of rays by the rank.

targets.target: Faces and products of regular cones are regular
targets.note: Products are for the product lattice map i.prodMap i'.

targets.target: Block form of the transition matrix between two extending bases
targets.note: Ray columns are standard columns and, for compatible splittings into rays and a common complement, the matrix is [[1,B],[0,D]] with D unimodular; needs IsIntegralLattice and salience.

targets.target: Finite fans of toric cones: definition, support, completeness
targets.note: Fan carries IsIntegralLattice, a finite set of toric cones, face closure and the left half of the intersection axiom (the right half is Fan.inf_isFaceOf_right).

targets.target: Open subfans, products of fans and subdivisions
targets.note: Subfans are face-closed subsets of cones; support_prod, isComplete_prod_iff, IsRegular.prod and IsSubdivision.refl/trans/prod are also proved. There is no star-subdivision construction.

targets.target: Fan morphisms with identity, composition and support functoriality
targets.note: FanHom stores the lattice map, the real map and the cone condition; the real map is forced (FanHom.realMap_eq). Also comp_id, id_comp, prodMap, fst/snd and leastCone.

targets.target: Dual affine semigroup of integral characters nonnegative on a cone and its finite generation (Gordan)
targets.note: No dual-semigroup construction and no Gordan lemma for rational cones. Mathlib has only the equalizer version for well-quasi-ordered monoids such as N^k (Submonoid.fg_eqLocusM, whose additive form is not indexed) and the predicate IsAffineAddMonoid (Mathlib/Algebra/AffineMonoid/Basic.lean line 20; its declarations.tsv row is misparsed with name 'abbrev').

targets.target: Face localization, functoriality and regular-coordinate equivalence N^k x Z^(n-k) of dual semigroups
targets.note: Nothing about dual semigroups exists, so none of these statements is present; only the extending-basis data and the generic contravariant map on complex points of a semigroup homomorphism.

targets.target: Affine toric scheme Spec C[S_sigma], link to a ToricVariety instance, dense torus and torus action
targets.note: Neither library has AlgebraicGeometry.ToricVariety or an affine-monoid toric-variety construction (these live only in the external Toric project). Tau Ceti has the diagonalizable group scheme D(G) = Spec R[G] for finitely generated commutative groups, a candidate dense torus, but no affine toric scheme and no torus action on one.

targets.target: Face inclusions give affine open immersions with identity, composition, overlap and cocycle laws
targets.note: Mathlib proves Spec S -> Spec R is an open immersion when S is a localization of R away from one element, and R[T,T^-1] is the localization of R[X] away from X (the ray-to-zero-cone case). The toric lemma that C[S_tau] is a localization of C[S_sigma] away from a character is absent.

targets.target: Gluing the affine schemes of a finite fan; global torus, action, cone opens, algebraic toric maps and their functoriality
targets.note: Mathlib's general and locally directed gluing of diagrams of open immersions fits the face poset of a fan, but no fan scheme, global torus action or toric morphism is built.

duplicates.note: Also works with rational polyhedral cones closed under faces with pairwise face intersections, refinements (subdivisions) and affine toric charts / torus embeddings, extended to arithmetic-admissible fans.

targets.target: Basis-free evaluation of integral characters on the complex torus, with multiplicative laws
targets.note: The torus is AddChar (N ->+ Z) Cˣ for a finite free Z-module N; characterEvaluation_zero is also proved.

targets.target: Separation of torus points by characters and compatibility with lattice maps
targets.note: complexTorusMap is covariant in N and evaluates by pulling characters back along the lattice map; complexTorusMap_id is also proved.

targets.target: Laurent-monomial formula for character evaluation after choosing a basis
targets.note: A free presentation of the character lattice gives ComplexTorus N = (sigma -> Cˣ) with coordinates equal to evaluation at the transported generators. Missing: the statement x(m) = prod_i x_i^(m_i) for an arbitrary character on ComplexTorus (it follows from freeAbelianCharEquiv_symm_apply_ofAdd; the scheme-level split torus has the Laurent-monomial statement).

targets.target: Contravariant map on affine complex points induced by a semigroup homomorphism, compatible with the monoid-algebra map
targets.note: Points are C-algebra maps C[Multiplicative S] -> C; comap precomposes with MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom. Works for any commutative additive monoids.

targets.target: Continuity of the induced map for monomial-embedding topologies, independent of chosen generators
targets.note: Continuity holds for arbitrary finite generating families on source and target; monoid isomorphisms give homeomorphisms.

targets.target: Typed mixed exponent data; preservation of the invertible torus-coordinate locus and holomorphy there
targets.note: MixedExponent has three blocks (N-valued boundary-boundary, Z-valued torus-boundary and torus-torus) and no boundary-to-torus block; mixedChartDomain is C^k x (C^*)^l inside C^k x C^l; holomorphy is ContDiffOn C of every order.

targets.target: Identity, composition on the mixed-chart locus, and products of mixed monomial maps
targets.note: Composition is proved only on mixedChartDomain, as the roadmap requires; the identity law holds at every ambient point.

targets.target: Jacobian formulas for mixed monomial maps
targets.note: Stated as the partial derivatives of the four coordinate blocks (the torus-variable ones on mixedChartDomain); no packaged Jacobian matrix or fderiv statement.

targets.target: Biholomorphicity of mixed monomial maps for inverse or unimodular block exponent data
targets.note: An OpenPartialHomeomorph between mixed-chart domains that is ContDiffOn C both ways, for two-sided inverse exponent data and for the block [[1,C],[0,D]] with D unimodular. It is not packaged as a Mathlib PartialDiffeomorph, but Tau Ceti's PartialDiffeomorph.ofOpenPartialHomeomorph does that in one step.

targets.target: Face localization is an open embedding of complex points and a biholomorphism onto its image
targets.note: No face-localization maps of dual semigroups exist, and nothing proves that comap along a localization has open image or is an embedding or biholomorphism.

targets.target: Cocycle equations for successive face inclusions
targets.note: Functoriality of comap gives the cocycle identity for any composable semigroup homomorphisms; missing are the face-inclusion maps of dual semigroups to which it would be applied.

targets.target: Monomial-embedding topology on affine complex points: independent of generators, Hausdorff, locally compact, second countable
targets.note: Proved for every commutative additive monoid with a finite generating family, not just dual semigroups of cones; the embedding is closed (isClosedEmbedding_monomialEmbedding) and its range is the binomial locus. The topology is a def depending on the family, not an instance.

targets.target: Biholomorphism of the regular affine chart with C^k x (C^*)^(n-k) from an extending basis, with character coordinates
targets.note: Nothing identifies the dual semigroup of a regular cone with N^k x Z^(n-k), or its complex points with the mixed chart; the generic homeomorphism for monoid isomorphisms and the mixed-chart model exist separately.

targets.target: Named complex ChartedSpace and IsManifold instance on a regular affine chart
targets.note: Only Mathlib's generic charted-space and manifold machinery; no toric chart structure in either library.

targets.target: Changing the extending basis preserves the complex structure via the mixed monomial biholomorphism
targets.note: The block form [[1,B],[0,D]] of a change of extending basis and the biholomorphism of C^k x (C^*)^l it induces are proved. Missing: the charts themselves and the proof that their transition map is this biholomorphism (so that the atlas does not depend on the basis).

targets.target: Dense torus as an open submanifold; face orbits as locally closed complex submanifolds with dimension and closure relation
targets.note: No orbit or torus-inclusion results for affine toric charts; only generic open-subset charted spaces, locally closed sets and smooth embeddings.

targets.target: Face localization is an open holomorphic embedding agreeing with complex points of the algebraic open immersion
targets.note: Neither the analytic face-localization embedding nor the algebraic open immersion of affine toric schemes exists.

targets.target: TopCat.GlueData of affine charts and face-localization overlaps, with symmetry and cocycle from the fan axioms
targets.note: Mathlib's gluing structures and Tau Ceti's fan intersection axiom exist, but no toric gluing diagram is built.

targets.target: Complex-manifold structure on TopCat.GlueData.glued; chart inclusions are open holomorphic embeddings compatible on overlaps
targets.note: Neither library has a complex-manifold gluing theorem (the README assigns it to the complex-manifolds roadmap); Mathlib only gives open embeddings of the pieces into a topological gluing and charted spaces pushed along surjective local homeomorphisms.

targets.target: Hausdorffness of the glued realization from the fan intersection property
targets.note: No separation criterion for glued spaces in Mathlib's Topology/Gluing, and no toric Hausdorffness statement; only chartwise Hausdorffness of affine complex points.

targets.target: Second countability, local compactness and finite dimensionality of the glued realization
targets.note: The chartwise facts are proved in Tau Ceti; the statements for the glued finite-fan space are absent.

targets.target: Invariance under fan equivalence, open-subfan functoriality, and the holomorphic map induced by a subdivision
targets.note: Only the combinatorial subfans, subdivision morphisms and fan-morphism composition exist; no analytic realization to act on.

targets.target: Glued torus action: group law, joint continuity, holomorphy, equivariance of chart inclusions and characters
targets.note: No action of the coordinate-free torus on affine complex points or on a glued realization in either library.

targets.target: Orbit-cone correspondence as an order-reversing equivalence; stabilizers and quotient tori from sublattices
targets.note: Only generic orbit/stabilizer vocabulary and the torus map induced by a lattice map.

targets.target: Ray-indexed invariant closed embedded hypersurfaces whose union is the complement of the dense torus, with reduced multiplicity one
targets.note: The finite ray index set and primitive generators exist; no boundary components, complex submanifolds or multiplicity statements.

targets.target: Local simple-normal-crossings form: regular chart at each point, components through it, complex local biholomorphism to coordinate hyperplanes
targets.note: mixedMonomialMap_fst_eq_zero_iff describes when a boundary coordinate of a mixed monomial image vanishes; there is no toric chart, boundary component or normal-form statement.

targets.target: Transversality, cone-indexed intersection formula, naturality under fan isomorphisms, products and open subfans
targets.note: Only the combinatorial fan operations exist.

duplicates.note: Also proves the normal-crossings description of the boundary of glued torus embeddings for a smooth fan (in toroidal compactifications).

targets.target: Glued mixed monomial map of a fan morphism: holomorphy, identity, composition, products, uniqueness from the dense torus
targets.note: The fan-morphism combinatorics (including the least target cone of each source cone) and the affine mixed-monomial calculus exist; the induced map on realizations does not.

targets.target: Cone-by-cone preimages of affine charts and orbit strata; restriction and base change for open subfans
targets.note: No realizations, charts or strata to take preimages of.

targets.target: Properness of the analytic toric map iff each target cone's real preimage equals the support of source cones mapped into it
